subject: Integration incident: CloudForge webhook failures & joint SLA coordination
messages:
From: Ashley Park <ashley@cloudforge.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: devops@cloudforge.com
Date: 2026-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Repeated webhook 500s and delayed callbacks — urgent

Hi Sean,

We started seeing a spike in 500s and multi-second callback latency to our webhook endpoints hitting your hosted inference on 2026-11-02 23:00 UTC. This is affecting our customer-facing inference pipeline (request ID batch attached) and causing retries from our side that cascade into higher concurrency.

Symptoms:
- ~12% 500 responses from /v1/infer/rf-infer-1 between 23:00-02:00 UTC
- Median callback latency jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s
- Errors correlate with payloads that include long system prompts + long context (we can share examples)

We attached a sample of our logs and request IDs (cloudforge_error_log_1103.zip). Can we get an urgent alignment on triage and a temporary mitigation path? Our customers are starting to open tickets.

We'd like to:
1) schedule an immediate troubleshooting call with your infra/serving team
2) confirm what SLA/response times Redwood can commit to during a Sev 2 impact
3) get a runbook (or quick mitigation) we can follow until permanent fix is deployed

Thanks — appreciate a quick response.

Ashley Park
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudForge Labs
ashley@cloudforge.com

--- Attachment: cloudforge_error_log_1103.zip (text/zip, ~2.1MB)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:03:24-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Repeated webhook 500s and delayed callbacks — urgent

Forwarding CloudForge incident — Ashley included logs. Can we triage this as partner escalation and coordinate an external-facing message?

High-level ask:
- Quick triage: is this a serving/kernel regression, cache pressure, or routing flap?
- Temporary mitigations: route CloudForge to a fallback model variant or lower concurrency, enable aggressive KV prefix caching?
- SLA handling: propose a short note to the partner with expected time to mitigation and a meeting time.

I'm available for a touch-base at 12:30 PT. Camila / Jonas, can you take technical lead? Marissa, please own the partner comms and share the meeting link.

Thanks,
Sean
VP of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-04T08:15:10-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Repeated webhook 500s and delayed callbacks — urgent

On Tue, Nov 3, 2026 at 11:03 AM Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Forwarding CloudForge incident — Ashley included logs. Can we triage this as partner escalation and coordinate an external-facing message?

Thanks for the heads up. Quick notes from my side after an initial glance at the logs:
- The 500s appear correlated with cache eviction patterns when sessions include very long prefixes + concurrent streaming sessions.
- Workaround options we can implement quickly (30–90 mins):
  * Route CloudForge traffic to a lower-memory model variant (rf-infer-1-lite) with identical API but smaller KV footprint
  * Temporarily bump prefix cache TTL for CloudForge customer tokens to reduce eviction thrash
  * Apply rate-limit back-pressure for retries (we can set a soft 80% concurrency cap)

Jonas — can you confirm if a quick TTL bump + soft throttle is safe for their contract tier? If so, we can enable as emergency mitigation and monitor.

I'll prepare a short triage checklist (joint_debug_steps.md) and attach to the post-call notes. We should also document an SLA addendum that defines response times for partner-impacting incidents; Marissa, can you draft and share with Ashley after we confirm the mitigation window?

Camila Reyes
Director, Partner Reliability
Redwood Inference
--- Attachment: joint_debug_steps.md (text/markdown, 6KB)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-04T12:42:56-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Repeated webhook 500s and delayed callbacks — urgent

Thanks — dug in more after reproducing with CloudForge sample payloads. Technical summary: 
- Root cause (likely): KV cache thrash combined with long prefix keys (their ingestion includes long system prompts). Under bursts of concurrent streaming, we observe disproportionate memory eviction and transient kernel OOM/500s.
- Short-term remediation (I can push these in the next maintenance window / emergency change):
  1) Increase KV cache capacity reserved for CloudForge tenant by +20% (hot fix, no restart).
  2) Apply a per-tenant prefix hash cap to limit effective prefix-length explosion (config change).
  3) Canary the change for 2 hours with 5% traffic first, then 100% if stable.

Estimated ETA: 2–4 hours to apply hotfix + monitoring dashboards to validate error rate and p50/p95 latency. Risk: minimal — changes are configuration-only.

I've assembled a compact note that we can share (sla_patch_notes.txt) outlining the planned changes and rollback steps. I'll be online for the call at 13:30 PT.

Jonas Weber
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
--- Attachment: sla_patch_notes.txt (text/plain, 3KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ashley Park <ashley@cloudforge.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, devops@cloudforge.com
Date: 2026-11-05T09:50:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Repeated webhook 500s and delayed callbacks — follow-up and meeting

Hi Ashley,

Thanks for flagging and for the logs — we reproduced the issue on our side and have a mitigation plan ready to implement. Apologies for the impact to your customers.

Proposed immediate plan:
- 09:30 PT today: apply KV cache reservation + prefix cap canary (5% traffic)
- Monitor for 2 hours; if stable, ramp to 100% and notify you
- If we see regressions, rollback within 15 minutes and open a post-mortem

Meeting: I scheduled a 30-minute triage/align call on 2026-11-05 at 10:00 PT — join here: https://meet.google.com/xyz-abcq-rst

I've attached a draft SLA addendum that captures expected response times and communication channels for partner-impacting incidents (sla_draft_cloudforge_v1.pdf). Please review and let me know if you'd like redlines during the call.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
--- Attachment: sla_draft_cloudforge_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 45KB)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ashley Park <ashley@cloudforge.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-07T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Repeated webhook 500s and delayed callbacks — post-triage summary & SLA next steps

Thanks everyone for the quick response and CloudForge for patience. Short summary and agreed next steps: 

What we did (2026-11-05):
- Applied KV cache reservation + prefix cap canary at 09:30 PT; monitored p50/p95 and 500-rate.
- After 2 hours of stability we ramped to full traffic; 500s dropped to baseline and median callback latency returned to ~140ms.

Agreed actions:
- Jonas to push the configuration as a permanent tenant reservation within the next 48 hours and add automated alerting for prefix-eviction spikes.
- Camila to finalize the triage checklist and publish to our partner runbook repo (joint_debug_steps.md -> published).
- Marissa to finalize SLA addendum and circulate for legal review; request: CloudForge to acknowledge and sign the addendum for the formal record.
- Sean to coordinate a 30-day follow-up to review stability metrics and discuss any broader capacity/quantization recommendations.

Ashley — appreciate you sending the logs. Can you and your team please confirm acceptance of the SLA addendum (sla_draft_cloudforge_v1.pdf) by EOD 2026-11-09? If we get sign-off, we'll bake the addendum into your partner contract and schedule the 30-day review.

If anything else is required, flag it here and we'll escalate.

Sean Gallagher
VP of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
